_note: Transcribed from the Barkla job logs on 2026-09-07 while the cluster was reachable. The authoritative files are dpo/run-<jobid>/result.json on fastscratch; re-sync them before quoting these numbers in the dissertation.

runs.reason: DPOConfig in trl 1.12 does not accept max_prompt_length; TypeError at construction. Fixed by filtering the config against DPOConfig's own dataclass fields.

runs.interpretation: Null result attributed to the metric, not the model: averaging over prompt+completion diluted the differing section by roughly an order of magnitude.

runs.metric: completion tokens only; summed and length-normalised
runs.interpretation: Summed accuracy of exactly 0/7 is pure length bias: chosen completions are systematically longer (median 7000 vs 5581 characters) and a summed log-probability is strictly more negative for a longer sequence. The length-normalised figure is the meaningful one and did not move, but accuracy over 7 discrete pairs takes values only in sevenths and cannot separate 'no effect' from 'an effect too small to flip a pair'. A continuous margin statistic was added afterwards and has NOT yet been run.

pending: scripts/dpo/train_dpo.py now reports a per-pair margin (length-normalised logprob of chosen minus rejected) alongside accuracy. Not yet deployed to the cluster or run.
limitations: n=7 held out admits no statistical claim; a binomial test at this size rejects p=0.5 only at 0/7 or 7/7.
trl emitted tokenizer-mismatch warnings on every pair, indicating the prompt/completion boundary does not tokenize cleanly.
The contribution demonstrated is the harvesting pipeline, not a performance improvement.
